title: Simple types cut out initial parts that are type-definable, discretely ordered and closed under minima
author: Predrag Tanović
work: Vaught's conjecture for theories of discretely ordered structures
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes what a simple type over a set A does to the witness order attached to it: the set P(M) = C union p(M) is an initial part that is type-definable over A, it sits inside an A-definable discretely ordered initial part, every relatively definable nonempty subset of it has a minimum, and two witnesses whose orders agree on C agree on all of P(M) (statement lines 138-148). The proof transfers formulas between C and p in each clause: the C-type property is what moves a formula satisfied on C up to the realisation a, and it is applied once for the initial-part claim, once for the discrete order, once for the minimum, while the last clause is a minimality argument inside P(M) (proof lines 151-171). The step that carries the content is the transfer in clause (c), since it converts a statement about the finite interval [c_0,c] into a statement about the possibly infinite interval below a; the other clauses reuse the same mechanism. H2.
